label: 1-2 steps after an early original-phase x
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase on the one or two tokens right after the letter x, but only early in the sequence (steps 1-4). It does not care which token is currently being input. The step right after x carries most of the mass (prev_tok=x has 17x lift and 76% of mass). The step two after x gets a smaller tail. Magnitude is largest when x sits at position 1 and the next step is also x (w x x q peaks at the q, about 4.0). A single x at position 1 gives about 0.64 of max on the next step, and x at position 0 gives about 0.42. It is almost silent at the delimiter (0.4% of mass), never fires in the copy phase, and does not fire after x at later positions (t >= 5). Missed activations are tiny (about 2.6% of mass) and scattered across early steps with no x.

issues: Minor: counted by steps, recall is only 0.754 on test. About 32.5k active steps are missed, but they carry 2.6% of the activation mass and are almost all very weak (coverage of the lowest activation quartile is 0.11). They are spread across early steps that have no x seen (~seen x & t<=4 gives P=0.012). Previous tokens o/1/e explain only 0.6% of the mass, so this is diffuse noise, not a second pattern.

Minor: the prev2==x part is less exact than the prev==x part. prev==x & t<=4 gives P=0.978. prev2==x without prev==x gives P=0.838, falling to P=0.758 at t==4. Most false positives are step 4 after an x at position 2 or 3, where the feature often stays silent. This fits the label's 'smaller tail' wording.

The claims check out. Copy phase has 0 active steps. Delimiter has 0.4% of mass (phase==1 P=0.002). For t>=5 after an x, prev==x gives P=0.053 and MR=0.004. t==1 after an x at position 0 gives P=1.0. The x,x at positions 1-2 case fires every time (P=1.0), and its mean mass per step is about 1.47x that of a single x at position 1, which matches the claimed ~0.64 of max.

Every top example starts with 'w x x', but the first-token w is not what drives it. The mean mass per step for x x at t=3 is the same with or without w at position 0, so the 'w x x q' example in the explanation is just an instance. Even so, describing the peak as being about w would be misleading.
Extending the time limit to t<=5 lowers F1 to 0.780, so t<=4 is the right cutoff. Adding an x three steps back (rel_tok(-3)) gives P=0.029, so it adds no signal.
